{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./br5_FPointNet.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   --time=0-72:00:00       -> -t 72h
#   --ntasks-per-node=32     -> -n 32 (assuming 1 node)
#   --gres=gpu:0             -> -g 0 (no GPUs requested)
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 32 -t 72h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm --job-name=br5_FPointNet not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  # NOTE: Slurm --partition=gpu not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the gpu partition.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mem=16G not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  # NOTE: Slurm --output/--error used %j expansion (jobid) which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: log filenames may not be unique unless you add uniqueness.

  # load cuda
  module load cuda

  # activate environment
  source ~/anaconda3/bin/activate ~/anaconda3/envs/3DOD_Env

  # locate to your root directory
  cd /home/jbandl2s/sub_ensembles/models || exit 1

  DATA_FILE="/scratch/jbandl2s/Lyft_dataset/artifacts/frustums_train"
  MODEL_LOG_DIR="./log_v1_test/"
  RESTORE_MODEL_PATH="./log_v1_test/model.ckpt"

  # Run within the allocation.
  flux run -n 32 python train_branch_15.py
fi
"
}

issues: This is a self-submitting pattern: it will only work if `flux batch` can connect to a Flux broker from where the script is executed (inside a Flux instance or via a site-provided submission endpoint).
The script requests no GPUs in Flux (and originally `--gres=gpu:0`), but it loads CUDA; if the workload actually needs GPUs, the allocation will be unsuitable (resource suitability concern).

No CPU core count (`-c`) is requested for the 32 tasks; depending on site defaults, each rank may get only 1 core and core binding may differ from the original intent (resource sizing/mapping concern).
